hints: Treat each parcel as a unit of flow through directed routes.
Each route has a capacity and a cost per unit.
Send k units using minimum-cost flow, or report failure if fewer can reach the destination.
analogy: Each route is a pipe with limited space and a price for each parcel using it.
example: Two parallel routes with capacities 1 and 2 and per-parcel costs 2 and 3 deliver 3 parcels for cost 8.
algorithm: Build a residual network with each route's capacity and cost and a reverse edge of opposite cost. Repeatedly find a cheapest residual path from city 1 to city n using shortest paths with potentials, augment by the minimum remaining demand and path capacity, and update residual capacities. Print -1 if no path exists before k units are sent.
correctness: Residual reverse edges allow previous routing decisions to be revised. Successive shortest augmenting paths preserve minimum cost for each achieved flow value, so reaching k units gives the cheapest delivery.
complexity: For n cities, m routes and k parcels, O(k*m log n) time with potentials and Dijkstra, and O(n+m) space.
